findings.highlight: given me the right to decide
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=わたし char=2]他人に決定権を委ねるべきじゃなかった
findings.governingReading: Rin says Shirou should not have entrusted decision-making authority to another person, with “me” supplied as the ruby reading.
findings.explanation: The English keeps only Rin as referent and deletes the broader other-person principle encoded by the written text.

findings.evidenceJa: 心臓が、一際大きく拡縮する
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s heart contracts and expands with exceptional force or amplitude.
findings.explanation: The English changes the heart’s physical expansion and contraction into audible loudness.

findings.governingReading: The object beside Shirou’s heart is a restraint called an oath.
findings.explanation: The English deletes both the restraint’s name and its conceptual connection to his vow.

findings.highlight: I fight the binding, hoping that it’s not too late
findings.evidenceJa: 一刻も早く動けるようにともがいて
findings.governingReading: Shirou struggles to make his body move again at the earliest possible instant.
findings.explanation: The English changes urgency of bodily recovery into fear that an unstated deadline has passed.

findings.highlight: because there’s no longer a need to hold me here
findings.evidenceJa: 反対していた理由が、既に失われたからではないのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou infers that his body became free because the reason he opposed Rin has already been lost—meaning Sakura may already be dead.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes an external need to restrain him, deleting the bad end’s devastating causal realization.

findings.highlight: lost the person on whom I’d depended
findings.governingReading: Shirou has lost that new anchor or point of support.
findings.explanation: The English concretizes the figurative support as a person and adds emotional dependence.
